author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Swedish defenseman John Klingberg announced his retirement Friday after 700 NHL regular-season games across six teams.

Klingberg, 34, spent his first eight NHL seasons with the Dallas Stars after the club selected him in the fifth round of the 2010 draft. He earned All-Rookie recognition in 2014-15 and was selected for the All-Star Game in 2017-18.

He finished with 443 regular-season points, including 92 goals and 351 assists, during stops with Dallas, Anaheim, Minnesota, Toronto, Edmonton and San Jose. Last season he recorded 27 points in 56 games for the Sharks. Klingberg also produced 43 points in 82 playoff games.

His postseason career included Stanley Cup Final appearances with Dallas in 2020 and Edmonton in 2025. Both series ended in six-game losses. Internationally, Klingberg helped Sweden win consecutive world championship gold medals in 2017 and 2018, adding major national-team success to a long 12-season NHL career as a mobile defenseman.
dek: The Swedish defenseman ends a career that included 443 regular-season points, an All-Star selection and two trips to the Stanley Cup Final.
headline: John Klingberg retires after 700 NHL games
